Gold price trades near $4,000/oz after final Consumer Sentiment holds steady at 48, inflation expectations rise
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market is trading near key support after the latest data showed consumer sentiment in the U.S. holding steady, while inflation expectations rose higher. The University of Michigan announced on Friday that the final reading of its Consumer Sentiment survey for October was 48. The data was better than expectations, as the consensus forecast of economists called for a reading of 46.3, the same as the preliminary reading, and it was also just below September’s final reading of 48.1. “Consumer sentiment held steady this month, registering a scant one-tenth of an index point below September,” said Surveys of Consumers Director Joanne Hsu in the report. “Increases in sentiment among Republicans and Democrats were balanced by declines among independents. While year-ahead business conditions improved about 14%, they stand 16% less than last October’s read.”

items.titleEn: Gold struggles as S&P PMI shows health activity in Manufacturing Services sectors
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market continues to hold support around $4,000 an ounce, but it could face further headwinds as relatively stable activity in both the manufacturing and services sectors reduces safe-haven demand for the precious metal. S&P Global reported on Friday that its flash Composite Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) fell to 57.6 in October, down from September’s reading of 58.4. “US business activity growth slowed in October but remained close to September’s recent high in response to a further improvement in order books. Growth rates in both manufacturing and services remained among the best seen over the past five years as robust domestic demand was accompanied by renewed signs of export growth,” the report said.

Gold heads for steep weekly loss as Hormuz tensions lift crude toward five-month highs - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in early U.S. trading Friday, extending Thursday's heavy losses as renewed Middle East tensions pushed crude oil prices higher and reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain restrictive monetary policy. Gold failed to attract sustained safe-haven demand despite growing geopolitical risks and weakness in global equities, while silver faced additional pressure from concerns about industrial activity and elevated borrowing costs. At the latest available morning price reading, spot gold was trading near $4,026.56 an ounce, down 2.40% on the quoted session, while spot silver was trading near $53.801, down 6.40%. Gold was heading toward a weekly loss of more than 3.5%, with both metals remaining under heavy selling pressure. Market positioning remains dominated by persistent inflation pressure and expectations for further monetary tightening. September consumer prices rose 0.6% on the month and 3.7% annually , while producer prices increased 1.3% and 6.3%, respectively. Interest rate futures indicate that the Fed is widely expected to leave rates unchanged at its Oct. 27-28 meeting, although traders continue to assign approximately a 78% probability to at least one additional increase by December. Thursday's sharp technology-led equity selloff encouraged demand for government bonds, producing a substantial decline in Treasury yields. However, the benchmark 10-year yield rebounded toward the 5.0% area Friday as renewed energy-price increases revived inflation concerns. The combination of firm rate expectations, rising crude prices and continued liquidation pressure has limited gold's ability to benefit from geopolitical uncertainty or intermittent declines in yields.
